espresso-bark.$description: Espresso Bark — Primary text, navigation background, structural borders — a warm near-black that anchors every screen without the harshness of pure #000000

terracotta-ember.$description: Terracotta Ember — Primary action borders, active nav state, decorative accents — rationed to moments of intent, never used as a large surface fill

iris-ink.$description: Iris Ink — Decorative display headings, logo monogram stroke — a vivid violet that breaks the warm palette for brand-voice headlines only

honey-parchment.$description: Honey Parchment — Subtle highlight washes, eyebrow label backgrounds, warm text tint — a muted yellow that warms the cream canvas without competing with terracotta

warm-linen.$description: Warm Linen — Page canvas, content section backgrounds — the dominant surface, never pure white, always slightly cream

ash-mist.$description: Ash Mist — Hairline borders, dividers, card edges — the most-used color on the site (1,300+ occurrences), creates the cool rule-lines that structure every layout

blush-cream.$description: Blush Cream — Warm tinted surface for hover states and soft callout blocks — a peach wash that warms the cream canvas

lilac-mist.$description: Lilac Mist — Cool surface accent for secondary panels — a lavender-tinted gray that introduces gentle contrast against the warm cream

carbon.$description: Carbon — True black used sparingly for image fills and footer text — Espresso Bark handles all structural dark needs

monasans.$description: Body text, navigation, buttons, section headings, UI labels — the workhorse sans-serif. Uppercase instances at 0.07-0.1em tracking are signature; the wide tracking on 12-14px labels reads like a museum placard, not a UI label.

paradigm-pro.$description: Display headings and hero text only — a whisper-thin custom serif at weight 300. The ultra-light weight is anti-convention: most editorial sites use 400-500 serifs for headlines, but this 300 creates authority through restraint. Tight line-height (0.95) lets the letters interlock like a logotype.
